lines.text: I ran to Halvard. I didn't know what I was going to do. I only knew what I needed.
Lord Kesting. Give me Kesting.
What?
The keep. The land. Your people. Let me claim it. I can't save what isn't mine.
Take it, boy. If you can save it.
I put both hands flat on the stones. Kesting's stones. Thirty men in green had watched farmers fight like knights all night. One by one, I felt them say yes.
Yrsa had taught me to let the cold pass through me, like wind through a house with two doors. That night, I opened every door at once.
It went out of me like a tide. Into every thread I had. All at once.
Every one of them. Every one of them is a ring higher. That's not possible. That's not...
Her lens cracked from edge to edge. She said the last thing it showed her was a net of light, thrown over the whole keep.
Farmers who had been threes fought like fours. Tobin threw a fallen gate at the wolves.
Oswin's frost froze a whole ramp of wolves where they climbed. For one night, the drunk the King had thrown out of his Third Company was a five.
Even Ash burned brighter.
And Wren. For one night, Wren was a five. She climbed the tower, and she drew, and the wind came with her arrow.
One arrow. Through the eye. The same way she had killed the bear that clawed Dunn, a lifetime ago.
All night we fought like that. And when dawn came, the frost began to go. It ran off the walls. It ran out of the pass. It went back north like the sea going out, and the beasts went with it.
Two hundred of His Majesty's soldiers. Alive. Because of a village.
The sun came up over Kesting. I remember Halvard's arms, and his beard full of melting frost.
Hold on, boy. Hold on. You saved it. Do you hear me? You saved it.
Then I didn't remember anything at all. For eight days.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter fifty-six, coming soon.
